hazards: Exposed copper strands can cause cuts or electrical shorts if plugged in. Older PVC insulation contains lead stabilizers and phthalates.
safe_handling: Unplug cables from all power sources before handling. Coil wires neatly and secure them with ties to prevent tangling.
unsafe_actions: Never burn plastic cable insulation to strip copper wires. Do not throw electronic cables into standard household trash bins.
what_to_do_if_damaged: Wrap frayed or exposed wires with electrical tape and immediately remove them from use to prevent shock or fire hazards.
disposal_route: Drop off at an authorized e-waste collection bin or certified electronic scrap recycler.
environmental_impact: Burning PVC cable coatings releases toxic hydrochloric acid gas and dioxins, while landfilling wastes valuable copper resources.
